newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold firm in Europe but latest gains may be capped.
newsitem.headline: Gold firm in Europe but latest gains may be capped.

text.p: Gold was up in early Europe, but may steady after sharp gains following an auditor's report Sunday which showed a major mine find is a hoax.
Gold began higher at $343.15/$343.65 an ounce versus $340.00/$340.50 in Europe early on Monday when U.K. banks were closed for a holiday. Gold closed Monday in New York at $342.50/$343.00.

The market was still focused on news published Sunday by an independent auditor which found that what was believed to be one of the richest finds of the century, a gold mine in Busang, showed no gold deposits of economic significance. Instead, the report showed test samples had been falsified.
"Longer-term it should have no influence," said one Swiss-based dealer of the report, adding however it created shock waves just after release.
Gold rose sharply on Monday in its wake.
The impact may be felt only indirectly if it makes it more difficult for small mines to find capital to fund exploration, he said.

"That could mean that gold production may not increase so much," the trader said. But, he added that while funds had covered short positions on Monday it appeared there were no longer big buyers this morning. In addition $343.00 was seen as resistance and gains above that may be difficult.
Other metals were also higher with silver at $4.76/$4.78 versus $4.70/$4.72 on Monday.
Platinum was firmer at $373.50/$374.50 versus $370.75/$371.75 and palladium was higher at $157.50/$158.50 versus $156.75/$157.75.
